property_summary: For every initialize(...) call, the contract's public baseToken equals the provided _baseToken argument (reference preserves input); the mutant that always sets baseToken to address(0) will violate this for any call where _baseToken != address(0).

For any caller and any _baseToken argument, calling initialize(...) sets c.baseToken() equal to the supplied _baseToken (the reference preserves the provided base token); the mutant that assigns baseToken = msg.sender will break this rule for callers where msg.sender != _baseToken.

After any initialize(...) call that succeeds, the stored nft address equals the _nft argument passed; the mutant assigns nft = _baseToken so for some inputs nft() != _nft and the property is violated.

For any initialize(...) inputs, the reference contract stores the provided _nft address in its public nft() state variable; the mutant sets nft to address(0) instead, so for some fuzzed _nft values the stored nft() will differ (i.e. equal to the supplied _nft) and the mutant will violate that.

For every initialize(...) call the contract stores changeFee equal to the supplied _changeFee (i.e., c.changeFee() == _changeFee); the mutant doubles the stored value so for some fuzzed _changeFee the equality breaks.
